name: The Punisher
notable_feat: Wages a one-man war on organized crime with no superpowers at all
why_underdog: Has a massive fan base but is constantly overshadowed by powered heroes despite relying purely on skill and grit

name: Moon Knight
powers_note: Power level fluctuates with the moon in some comic depictions
notable_feat: Went toe-to-toe with Werewolf by Night and led his own vigilante network
why_underdog: Only gained mainstream recognition after his 2022 Disney+ show, despite decades of comic history

name: Hawkeye
notable_feat: Has led the Avengers and even briefly wielded Thor's hammer
why_underdog: Frequently the punchline for having 'no powers' on a team of gods and super-soldiers

name: She-Hulk
notable_feat: Has held her own against Hulk-level threats while keeping full control of her mind
why_underdog: Matches or exceeds her cousin's power but rarely gets equivalent screen time or story focus

name: Ghost Rider
notable_feat: Can judge and punish the guilty with a single terrifying stare
why_underdog: Iconic visual design but rarely included in major team crossover storylines

name: Squirrel Girl
first_appearance: Marvel Super-Heroes Vol. 2 #8 (1991) (also known as the Marvel Super-Heroes Winter Special)
notable_feat: Has defeated Doctor Doom, Thanos, and Wolverine in the comics
why_underdog: One of the most quietly powerful characters in Marvel, played almost entirely for comedy

name: Nightcrawler
notable_feat: Infiltrated the White House solo, teleporting past the entire Secret Service
why_underdog: A fan favorite among X-Men readers but frequently sidelined in film adaptations

name: Jubilee
notable_feat: One of the longest-running X-Men characters despite minimal spotlight
why_underdog: Iconic 90s design and mascot status, but rarely given serious storylines

name: Machine Man
first_appearance: 2001: A Space Odyssey #8 (1977, as Mister Machine)
notable_feat: A Jack Kirby creation with cosmic-tier tech abilities
why_underdog: Virtually unknown outside dedicated comic readers despite a unique power set

name: Darkhawk
notable_feat: A cult-favorite 90s hero with a loyal but small fanbase
why_underdog: Almost no modern-day presence despite passionate nostalgia from longtime fans

name: Nova
notable_feat: Served as a member of the Nova Corps, wielding near-limitless cosmic power
why_underdog: One of Marvel's most powerful cosmic heroes, yet virtually unknown outside comics

name: Sleepwalker
notable_feat: Exists as an interdimensional being who can only act through a human host
why_underdog: A bizarre, unique concept from the 90s that has almost entirely faded from modern comics

name: Prowler
notable_feat: A Spider-Man ally with his own gadget-based arsenal
why_underdog: Rarely gets stories independent of Spider-Man despite a strong individual concept

name: U.S.Agent
notable_feat: Briefly served as Captain America before forging his own identity
why_underdog: Constantly compared to Captain America rather than judged on his own merits

name: Stature
first_appearance: Young Avengers #1 (2005, as Stature; Cassie Lang appeared earlier as a child in Marvel Premiere #47, 1979)
notable_feat: A core member of the Young Avengers with a strong legacy-hero arc
why_underdog: Overshadowed by her father Ant-Man despite a compelling story of her own

name: Speedball
first_appearance: Amazing Spider-Man Annual #22 (1988); his formal origin story and solo series continued shortly after in Speedball #1 (1988)
notable_feat: Underwent a dramatic transformation into the darker hero Penance
why_underdog: A key figure in Marvel's Civil War storyline, but rarely remembered outside it

name: Darkstar
notable_feat: A founding member of Soviet Super-Soldiers, one of Marvel's few Cold War-era heroes
why_underdog: Rarely used since her original era, despite a unique power set and origin

name: Silverclaw
notable_feat: A Young Avengers-adjacent hero with roots in South American mythology
why_underdog: One of the most obscure heroes with an interesting cultural background, rarely explored

name: Gravity
notable_feat: Created specifically as a modern homage to classic Silver Age heroes
why_underdog: Designed to be an underdog hero from the start, yet still barely appears in modern comics

name: Elsa Bloodstone
notable_feat: A monster hunter with a cult following through Nextwave and Marvel Zombies
why_underdog: Beloved by a niche fanbase but rarely appears in mainstream storylines or adaptations

name: Daredevil
notable_feat: Runs Hell's Kitchen as a blind lawyer by day and vigilante by night
why_underdog: Beloved by fans but consistently overshadowed by cosmic-scale Marvel heroes

name: Iron Fist
notable_feat: Defeated the dragon Shou-Lao to earn his signature power
why_underdog: Often criticized or overlooked despite a rich mystical martial arts mythology

name: Luke Cage
notable_feat: Marvel's first Black superhero to headline his own ongoing series
why_underdog: A foundational hero whose historical importance is often undercredited

name: Mockingbird (originally Huntress)
notable_feat: A former S.H.I.E.L.D. agent and skilled Avengers-level tactician
why_underdog: Frequently defined by her relationship to Hawkeye rather than her own career

name: Falcon
notable_feat: Marvel's first mainstream African American superhero, later became Captain America
why_underdog: Took decades to get mainstream recognition despite a long, significant history

name: War Machine
first_appearance: Iron Man #118 (1979, as James Rhodes); as War Machine in Iron Man #282 (1992)
notable_feat: Piloted a heavily armed variant of the Iron Man suit into major conflicts
why_underdog: Constantly living in Iron Man's shadow despite his own distinct arsenal and story

name: Vision
notable_feat: An android Avenger capable of phasing through solid matter
why_underdog: A powerful and philosophically rich character who rarely leads his own stories

name: Quicksilver
notable_feat: One of Marvel's fastest characters, rivaling speedsters from other universes
why_underdog: Frequently defined by his relationship to Scarlet Witch rather than his own arcs

name: Beast
notable_feat: A founding X-Man and one of Marvel's leading scientific minds
why_underdog: A founding member of the X-Men who rarely gets top billing in adaptations

name: Cannonball
notable_feat: Led multiple young mutant teams including the New Mutants
why_underdog: A longtime team leader who rarely gets solo recognition

name: Sunspot
notable_feat: Rose from New Mutant to head of the Hellfire Club and Avengers benefactor
why_underdog: A rare wealthy mutant leader whose business/hero double life is rarely explored

name: Rocket Raccoon
notable_feat: A genetically engineered creature who became a galaxy-saving weapons expert
why_underdog: Gained popularity mainly through film, with decades of comic history overlooked

name: Groot
notable_feat: One of Marvel's oldest characters, predating most major superheroes
why_underdog: Existed since 1960 as an obscure monster character before mainstream fame

name: Adam Warlock
notable_feat: One of the most powerful cosmic beings in Marvel, tied to the Infinity Gems
why_underdog: Despite immense power, rarely appears outside cosmic-focused storylines

name: Silver Surfer
notable_feat: Wields the Power Cosmic, one of the strongest forces in the Marvel Universe
why_underdog: One of Marvel's most powerful beings, yet rarely central to major crossover events

name: Blade
notable_feat: Has hunted vampires for decades, predating Marvel's mainstream horror boom
why_underdog: Rarely integrated into mainstream Avengers-level storylines despite iconic status

name: Iron Man 2020
notable_feat: An alternate Stark family armored hero from a dystopian future (Earth-8410) concept
why_underdog: A niche variant character almost entirely unknown outside dedicated readers. Unlike the heroic Tony Stark, the original 1984 version of Iron Man 2020 was introduced as a mercenary and corporate-driven antihero.

name: Firestar
first_appearance: 1981 tv series Spider-Man and His Amazing Friends; Spider-Man and His Amazing Friends #1 (1981)
notable_feat: A founding member of the New Warriors and an Avenger
why_underdog: Best known from a 1980s cartoon, often overlooked in modern comics

name: Justice
notable_feat: A founding New Warrior with strong telekinetic combat feats
why_underdog: Rarely appears outside team books despite consistent long-term presence

name: Triathlon
notable_feat: Joined the Avengers as part of a diversity-focused roster expansion
why_underdog: One of the most obscure former Avengers members in modern comics

name: Wiccan
notable_feat: A Young Avenger with power potentially rivaling his namesake, Scarlet Witch
why_underdog: Immense power potential largely unexplored outside Young Avengers stories

name: Hulkling
notable_feat: A hybrid Kree-Skrull heir with major galactic political significance
why_underdog: Ties to major cosmic bloodlines rarely explored outside niche team books

name: Patriot
powers: Superhuman strength and durability (temporary, later permanent)
notable_feat: Grandson of the original Black super-soldier Isaiah Bradley
why_underdog: Carries a historically important legacy that's rarely spotlighted

name: Songbird
notable_feat: A reformed villain who became a leader within the Thunderbolts
why_underdog: A compelling redemption arc largely unknown outside Thunderbolts readers

name: Ms. Marvel
first_appearance: Captain Marvel Vol. 7 #14 (2013); own title Ms. Marvel #1 (2014)
notable_feat: Marvel's first Muslim American character to headline her own series
why_underdog: Despite critical acclaim, took years to reach the mainstream audience she deserved

name: Spider-Woman
notable_feat: Predates Spider-Gwen and other spider-themed heroes by decades
why_underdog: Frequently confused with or overshadowed by newer spider-themed characters

name: Black Knight
notable_feat: Wields a cursed sword capable of cutting through nearly anything
why_underdog: A longtime Avenger whose mystical weapon storyline rarely takes center stage

name: Living Lightning
notable_feat: Served on multiple Avengers rosters as a fully energy-based being
why_underdog: A unique energy-based hero with almost no mainstream visibility

name: Blue Marvel
first_appearance: Adam: Legend of the Blue Marvel #1 (2008)
notable_feat: One of the most powerful heroes in Marvel, hidden from the public for decades
why_underdog: Deliberately written as historically overlooked in-universe, mirrored by his real-world obscurity

name: Captain Britain
notable_feat: Protector of the entire multiverse in his role tied to the Captain Britain Corps
why_underdog: A multiversally important hero with minimal recognition outside UK-focused stories
